decision: scoped this run to Phase 1 of the brief only
why: the brief says begin with Phase 1 and later phases depend on the CRDT core

decision: defined done as go test -race green plus live convergence of real WebSocket clients over real Postgres
why: a passing unit suite alone would not prove the services work together

decision: chose high rigor for the CRDT and its wire format
why: the ID ordering and snapshot format are hard to change once data is stored

decision: ran Postgres 17 in docker compose on port 55432 for integration tests
why: tests must hit a real database, not a mock

decision: asked two other models to sketch the design independently before coding
why: the RGA layout and GC rule are one-way doors worth designing twice

decision: switched the RGA from a linked list to a parent-pointer tree with ID-sorted children
why: the tree's text is fixed by the set of nodes, so replicas converge even with bad clocks; the list needed valid Lamport clocks to converge

decision: kept Lamport clocks over Grok's gapless per-client counters
why: with per-client counters a new insert can sort after older siblings and appear in the wrong place

decision: kept GC to tombstones with no children whose insert and delete are covered by the stable vector
why: both sketches showed that moving a tombstone's children to its parent reorders text

decision: made the op log idempotent with a unique key on each op ID
why: a retried append must not double count toward the 100-op snapshot cadence

decision: kept JSONB snapshots as the brief mandates despite Grok preferring bytea
why: the brief names JSONB explicitly; size cost goes to the user as an open decision

decision: rejected GPT's split between gap-free op sequence numbers and Lamport node IDs
why: one hub with ordered sockets gives per-client FIFO, so a single Lamport ID per op is enough

decision: rejected payload-only GC; library removes leaf tombstones under a caller-supplied stable vector, services do not call it yet
why: clearing a 4-byte rune saves nothing; replica membership for offline clients is a later-phase protocol

decision: made the server reject ops whose parent or target it does not hold
why: every honest client op depends on ops the server already has, and buffering unknown parents lets a bad client grow memory

decision: committed module, protos, generated code, migration, Makefile, compose
why: workers' diffs need a clean base to review against

decision: split the build into crdt (GPT), document-service (Grok), collab-hub (Grok) running in parallel on disjoint directories against a fixed API
why: the three units only share the API in specs/crdt.md and go.mod, which I pre-filled

decision: reviewed the crdt diff and reran its suite myself
why: a worker's summary is not evidence

decision: added a test that replicas with and without GC converge on edits made after the stable point
why: the worker skipped the one test that exercises the GC safety argument

decision: broke the leaf-only GC rule on purpose to check the new test catches it
why: a test that passes against broken code proves nothing
evidence: mutation run: FAIL with nil deref on seed 0, restored

decision: rewrote FuzzApply to mix inserts, deletes, and branching parents and fail on any rejected valid op
why: the original only built chains and returned early on errors, hiding failures

decision: committed the crdt unit
why: unit verified on its own before services build on it

decision: ran go mod tidy myself after the worker found pre-added deps marked indirect and a missing go.sum entry
why: go.mod is the lead's file; the worker correctly refused to edit it

decision: reviewed append.go, store.go, main.go and reran the suite against real Postgres
why: trust the artifact, not the summary

decision: left one-row-per-roundtrip inserts and snapshot rebuild under the row lock as is
why: fix only if the 100-editor load test shows them

decision: found that Leave, ops, and cursors looked up the hub by document ID after join
why: after a fail-stop a stale Leave could drop the refcount of the replacement hub and stop it under live clients

decision: wrote a regression test for the stale Leave before fixing it
why: show the bug is real, then show it gone

decision: made Join return a Session bound to the joined hub and routed all later messages through it
why: the hub a client joined is the only one that should hear from it

decision: ran the two-client acceptance test against real race-built binaries and Postgres, including restarting both services
why: Phase 1 acceptance is two clients converging; restart proves state is durable

decision: ran the 100-editor load test: convergence held but op round trip p99 was 24.8s under -race
why: the brief targets p99 under 50ms

decision: built e2e binaries with -race only when the test runs with -race
why: the race detector roughly doubled latency and hid the real baseline

decision: captured non-race baseline: 200 ops/s, p50 6.3s, p99 13.5s; one AppendOperations costs mean 4.5ms
why: a serial hub at 4.5ms per append caps at about 220 ops/s, matching the measured 200

decision: chose group commit in the hub plus a single-statement insert in document-service
why: the cost is a fixed per-transaction overhead paid once per keystroke, which batching amortizes

decision: relaunched the group-commit worker with the spec inlined in its prompt
why: the first worker read the spec path before the file write landed (file mtime matched its finish time) and correctly refused to guess

decision: accepted group commit plus unnest insert
why: p50 dropped from 6.3s to about 8ms and throughput from 200 to about 575 ops/s; my reruns put p99 at 284, 139, 47, 132, 36, 42ms so the worker's single 46.7ms was a lucky draw
evidence: 6 lead reruns of TestHundredConcurrentEditors (3 plain, 3 with the hub Append probe)

decision: move snapshot compaction off the Append transaction into a background per-document compactor
why: Postgres slow log showed no statement over 20ms under load; a hub-side probe showed the slow appends are exactly the snapshot appends, growing 16ms at 1000 ops to 37ms at 4000 ops, O(document) on every hundredth keystroke; caching the doc only halves it and stays O(document) on the hot path

decision: accepted background compaction, replaced the worker's repeatable-read retry loop with lock-free READ COMMITTED compaction, kept serve errors exiting 1
why: repeatable read made every concurrent append abort compaction and each retry redid O(document) work; ops and snapshots are immutable so isolation buys nothing; worker's main.go change had silently turned serve failure into exit 0
evidence: 8 load runs: p99 under 50ms in 7, one run 71ms with a 228ms max stall; race suite green

decision: pushed main to origin as a fast-forward (4697e6e..c7561f4) and added an Opus 5.5 review beside the Grok one
why: user asked for a direct push to main and flexible model choice; claude-opus-5-thinking-high is unavailable and opus-5-5 is the closest judgment model

decision: fix 12 review findings in two parallel workers split by directory; dismiss or defer the rest
why: fix: missing-snapshot fallback (both reviewers), Join ghost peer, slow-consumer socket left open, MaxUint64 clock, archived rejoin loop, GC precondition and collected-delete pending, compaction retry, rejected-op divergence, hub Load timeout, fan-out latency on a 20k-rune doc. dismiss: append-timeout ops lost (the replacement hub reloads committed ops from Postgres). defer as notes: registry Close not waiting on hub loops, Merge atomicity (test-only), open/close lifecycle RPCs, tests/crdt and tests/load folder names

decision: accepted both fix passes; reverted Ready() validation in crdt; added Replica.InsertAfter/Delete and cursor typists in the load test
why: Ready validating ops would turn invalid ops into MISSING_DEPENDENCY at the hub; profile showed the random-index harness spent 54% CPU in IDAt, which is client cost the brief's ID-based cursors avoid
evidence: pprof of e2e.test; full race suite green

decision: record the fan-out p99 tail as unproven on this laptop; proving it is Phase 5 in the brief
why: snapshots-off and synchronous_commit-off runs keep the tail; server Append p99 about 20ms; run-to-run spread 23ms to 761ms points at host contention
